title: TurnProvenance
description: v2 (2026-07-29): what served one turn — read via GET /api/models/turns/<turn_id>/provenance, rendered as the per-turn detail the conversation surface reveals on demand (spec §4.5). Frozen in v2 because the spec promises per-turn inspectability and a promise with no interface cannot be implemented consistently: this file is where that promise says what it means. Distinct from resolution-event.schema.json, which is the account-wide 最近切换 feed keyed on state CHANGES; this is keyed on a TURN and always exists, switch or not. Storage is the implementing lane's decision, with one constraint: written when the turn resolves and readable after the process exits — 'which source paid for this turn' is a billing question the user asks days later. Same redaction invariant as every other payload here: ids and i18n keys, never credential material or raw upstream error bodies. SHAPE RULING (07-29, review round 2): the winning attempt lives in `served` and NOWHERE ELSE, so 'at most one attempt served' and 'the served attempt is last' are not invariants a validator or a test has to defend — they are unrepresentable. Round 1 had one `attempts` array carrying an `outcome` per item, which let a payload claim two winners, a winner in the middle, or a top-level projection naming a source the array never mentions. The full attempt sequence is still recoverable, in order, as `failed_attempts` ++ [`served`].

turn_id.description: The turn this describes, in whatever id space the session store already uses. Opaque here — this contract does not invent a new identifier.

ts.description: When the turn resolved (served or gave up), not when it started.

requested_model_id.description: What the caller asked for, as the caller-facing MENU identifier (prefixed for open menus) — before mapping. Recorded because 「我选的模型」 and 「实际跑的模型」 differing is precisely what the user is inspecting.

outcome.description: How the turn ended, as one field instead of something the reader infers by comparing two others. served = some attempt produced output. exhausted = every attempt failed (`failed_attempts` non-empty, `served` null). no_candidate = the pipeline never tried anything (`failed_attempts` EMPTY, `served` null) because this (agent, model) chain had nothing runnable — an empty chain, or every member cooling / needs_action. The third case is the reason `failed_attempts` has no minItems: a turn that gave up before touching a source is exactly the turn the user most needs to inspect, so fabricating a phantom attempt to satisfy a schema would corrupt the record it exists to preserve.

failed_attempts.description: Every candidate that was tried and did NOT serve, in the order it was tried. May be empty (see `outcome: no_candidate`). Candidates SKIPPED before being tried (cooling, ineligible, needs_action) are not attempts and are absent — the chain query answers 'what else exists'. Every item here failed, by construction: there is no per-item outcome to disagree with the top level.

resolved_model_id.description: The id actually sent upstream for this attempt, mapping applied.

reason.description: Why this attempt failed, from the resolution-event `reason` vocabulary narrowed to the failure causes. NOT nullable and NOT free text: a failed attempt with no reason was the round-1 shape's other unrepresentable-should-have-been, and the classification already exists adapter-side (S1 gap ①). Param/protocol/tool-compat errors never appear here — they surface to the caller instead of producing a fallback (spec §4.3 step 3).

served.description: The attempt that produced the turn's output — the record of the winner, not a projection of it. NULL for both failure outcomes. Carries the same fields as a failed attempt minus `reason`, so the render walks `failed_attempts` then appends this one.

model_supply_state.description: v2 (07-29, review round 2): why nothing was tried, as the MODEL-SCOPED supply state of this (agent, requested_model) chain — `waiting` when every chain member is cooling and the turn would have succeeded later unattended, `interrupted` when the chain is empty or every member needs the user. Non-null IFF `outcome` is `no_candidate`; null otherwise, on the same pattern as `retry_at` in agent-chain.schema.json. Deliberately NOT the agent-level `supply_status` rollup from agent-supply.schema.json: that rollup answers for the backend's CURRENT model, and a turn can request a different one (see api.md → probe, same distinction). Same three-class taxonomy, evaluated at the (agent, model) grain — 「稍等即可」 and 「需处理」 are different answers and the turn record must not blur them.
